note: Majority: Minors Act 1950 (consolidated text on bermudalaws.bm), section 2: a minor is a person who hasn't reached eighteen; the Act's rules on minors' contracts and marriage settlements aren't held. Work: Employment of Children and Young Persons Act 1963 (consolidated), section 1: a child is a person under thirteen and a young person one under eighteen who is no longer a child; section 3: no child may be employed in any employment whatsoever, save light agricultural, horticultural or domestic work for a parent or guardian and light carrying by hand; section 5: no one below the upper limit of compulsory school age may work in school hours or for more than two hours on a school day; section 6: under fifteen, not in an industrial undertaking or on a vessel (save light errands and training); section 7: under eighteen, not at night (from sixteen until midnight). So the general age is 13, with 15 for industry and vessels. Performers: section 3 names no exception or licence for performing, so barred under thirteen (my reading). Service: Defence Act 1965 (consolidated), section 4 as replaced by the Defence Amendment Act 2018 (2018 : 33, in force 1 July 2018): the Royal Bermuda Regiment is raised by voluntary enlistment, and compulsory enlistment (conscription) is abolished; none.

sources.title: Bermuda Laws Online: Minors Act 1950 (consolidated)
sources.said: “minor” means a person who has not attained the age of eighteen years

sources.title: Bermuda Laws Online: Employment of Children and Young Persons Act 1963 (consolidated)
sources.said: “child” means a person under the age of thirteen years ... No child shall be employed in any employment whatsoever ... no child or young person under the age of fifteen years, shall be employed in any industrial undertaking, or in or upon any vessel other than a vessel where only members of his family are employed.

sources.title: Bermuda Laws Online: Defence Act 1965 (consolidated)
sources.said: The regiment shall be raised and maintained by means of voluntary enlistment. (2) For the avoidance of doubt, compulsory enlistment (conscription) is hereby abolished in Bermuda, on the coming into operation of the Defence Amendment Act 2018.
